findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Build `replace_with_retry`'s backoff on the existing `rebar._store.git_locking._backoff_sleep` / `_jitter` seam (lazy-imported, as fsutil does with its lock helpers) instead of a bare `time.sleep`, or say in the plan why jitter and the shared sleep seam are deliberately left out.
evidence: src/rebar/_store/git_locking.py:84-94 — `def _jitter(delay)` ('so competing processes de-synchronize instead of thundering in lockstep') and `def _backoff_sleep(seconds)` ('behind one seam so a test can measure rebar's deliberate latency')
src/rebar/_store/lock.py:32 — `from rebar._store.gitutil import _backoff_sleep, _jitter` (already reused in _store)
git_locking.py imports only stdlib plus `rebar._store.git_outcome`, and fsutil already lazily imports sibling `_store` modules (fsutil.py:45), so reuse adds no import cycle
Plan Testing: 'a persistent `PermissionError` re-raises after the deadline (patched to a short value)' — with no sleep seam, this test burns real wall-clock time
findings.finding: The helper's backoff is written as a bare, unjittered `time.sleep` with a fixed '10 ms doubling, capped at 100 ms' schedule. But `rebar._store` already has a bounded-backoff toolkit for this purpose: `git_locking._backoff_sleep` (a patchable sleep seam) and `git_locking._jitter` (uniform scaling from 0.75 to 1.25 'so competing processes de-synchronize instead of thundering in lockstep'). `lock.py` and `gitutil.py` already reuse both. Writing a third private sleep/backoff loop skips the jitter that exists to stop peers retrying in lockstep. It also gives tests no sleep seam to patch, so the deadline test runs real sleeps.
findings.location: Approach — 'retries `os.replace` on `PermissionError` with a short backoff (10 ms doubling, capped at 100 ms)'; Portability — 'it uses only `os.replace` and `time.sleep`'
scenarios: Several Windows writers (e.g. the sidecar or cursor tests with more than 2 threads) all lose the rename at once. With identical unjittered 10/20/40 ms gaps they retry at the same moments and collide again.
The helper deadline unit test has to really sleep, because only `time.sleep` is available and there is no `_backoff_sleep` to patch.
findings.suggested_fix: In `replace_with_retry`, lazily do `from rebar._store.git_locking import _backoff_sleep, _jitter` and sleep `_backoff_sleep(_jitter(min(0.01 * 2**n, 0.1)))` between attempts. Keep the 2 s deadline as a module constant. In the helper tests, patch `_backoff_sleep` so no real time passes.

findings.finding: The retry widens the window in which an older snapshot can be published over a newer one. A writer whose replace fails is retried up to 2 s later and then overwrites whatever the competing writer published. For monotonic state such as the review-bot cursor, last_pass and get_rotation, a delayed stale publish could regress the stored value. Previously the stale write would have been dropped with an error. The plan does not state that these consumers tolerate last-writer-wins with a stale late writer.
findings.location: Approach: route list (`atomic_write` covering the cursor, `reconciler/last_pass.py:285`, `reconciler/get_rotation.py:105`)
scenarios: Thread A computes cursor=10 and thread B computes cursor=12. B's rename lands; A's first replace hits WinError 5 and its retry succeeds, so the cursor regresses to 10 and items are reprocessed.

findings.finding: The premise 'The barrier tests intercept the replace step; a retried replace would wait on the barrier a second time' is false for tests/unit/test_plan_review.py. Its barrier patches `Path.replace` (monkeypatch.setattr(Path, "replace", barriered_replace), line 1324).
